_: Every label prefix these documents use, what it means, and who owns it.
The labels are how a spec cites itself -- "R1 says the workspace is a jail",
"blocked on T3" -- and until this file nothing anywhere said what an R or an
AC is. The convention lived entirely in the practice of whoever wrote the last
document, which is how two people end up meaning different things by the same
prefix without either of them being wrong.
It is also the authority the index defers to. `state.py` used to drop any
namespace the corpus never defined -- a rule derived from the corpus rather
than declared by a person. That is a patch: it made `UTF-8` disappear, and it
would have made a REAL foreign label disappear the same silent way, since a
label defined in another repository is indistinguishable from a typo when the
only evidence considered is this repository. The declaration replaces it, and
the test suite is what turns an undeclared prefix into a red instead of a
vanishing act.
Three fields, and each one is load-bearing:
means       a short noun phrase, lowercase. What a reader should understand
the label to be.
defined_in  globs where its definitions live. REQUIRED when authority is
"self", and verified: a definition found outside these globs
fails the suite, so the field cannot rot into decoration.
authority   "self" when this repository defines them; the name of the
repository that does when it does not; "none" when the prefix
is not a label at all.
Measured 2026-08-24 by walking the corpus: T 82 mentions, AC 17, R 16, UTF 3.
Those four are every label-shaped prefix these documents contain.

UTF.means: not a label - the character encoding UTF-8 matches the label shape exactly, one to four capitals and a hyphen and a digit
